item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5 with new pricing and subscription credits
item.description:
Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5 with new pricing and subscription credits

🔍 Overview

  • Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, promoted as a fast, low‑cost model.

💰 Pricing

Model Token range Input price (per 1 M tokens) Output price (per 1 M tokens)
Claude Haiku 5.5 ≤ 100 k $0.10 $0.50
Claude Haiku 5.5 > 100 k $0.50 $2.50
GPT‑6 Luna ≤ 272 k $0.10 $0.50
GPT‑6 Luna > 272 k $0.20 $0.75
  • Haiku 5.5’s base price matches OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Luna up to 100 k tokens.
  • Beyond that limit Haiku 5.5’s price rises five‑fold, while Luna’s increase is less steep.

🧮 Tokenizer & Hidden Cost

  • Haiku 5.5 uses a new, less generous tokenizer.
  • The same long prompt consumes about 1.25 × more tokens with Haiku 5.5 than with Haiku 4.5, creating a hidden price increase.

⚙️ Reasoning Levels

  • Haiku 5.5 defaults to medium reasoning and does not allow disabling reasoning.
  • Example runs using the llm CLI:
    • Low‑effort pelican SVG: 0.0936 cents, 7 seconds.
    • Max‑effort pelican SVG (includes a reasoning trace): 3.3826 cents, 5 minutes 9 seconds.

📊 Comparison to Haiku 4.5

  • Haiku 4.5 (which lacked reasoning levels) generated a pelican SVG for 0.7583 cents.

🛠️ Tooling Improvements

  • The latest llm-anthropic release removes the need to ship a new plugin version for each model. 
    1
2
3

    llm install -U llm-anthropic
llm anthropic refresh
llm -m claude-haiku-5.5 "Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle" -o thinking_effort low

📦 Additional Anthropic Updates

  • Cache‑read price for Sonnet 5.5 has been halved.
  • New API credit scheme (credits equal the subscription cost):
    Plan Monthly credit
    Max 5x users $100
    Max 20x users $200
    Team subscribers up to $500 (pooled)
  • Credits do not roll over; unused credits are forfeited.
  • Option to disable auto‑reload for the API; requests stop when the balance runs out.

📈 Cost Perspective Above 100 k Tokens

  • Above 100 k tokens, GPT‑6 Luna offers a better deal because its price increase is smaller than Haiku 5.5’s.

#Anthropic #ClaudeHaiku #AIpricing #LLM #APICredits

Source: Claude Haiku 5.5

item.title: Google Gemini model access shifted to paid tiers starting Oct 9
item.description:
Google Gemini model access shifted to paid tiers starting Oct 9

Starting on October 9th, Google Gemini’s free tier will be limited to the Flash Lite model.

🔍 Overview

  • Free users previously could choose Gemini Flash Lite, Flash, and Pro.
  • Access to the standard Flash model now requires a $4.99/month Google AI Plus subscription.
  • The AI Plus tier will soon lose Gemini Pro access.
  • AI Plus subscribers will be notified by email when they lose access.
  • Users can still select low, medium, or high effort levels for each model, though higher effort levels may consume usage limits faster.

⚙️ Model Access Changes

Model Required subscription Monthly price
Gemini Flash Lite Free plan —
Gemini Flash Google AI Plus $4.99
Gemini Pro / Deep Think Google AI Pro or Ultra $19.99 or $99.99

📅 Availability

  • The restriction to Flash Lite for free users begins on October 9.
  • After the change, only paid tiers will retain access to Gemini Flash and Pro models.

💡 Why it matters

  • Free users lose the ability to run higher‑performance Gemini models without paying.
  • The top‑tier Gemini Pro model and the “Deep Think” advanced reasoning option become exclusive to higher‑cost subscriptions, potentially reshaping how individuals and developers budget for AI usage.

#GoogleGemini #AIpricing #SubscriptionUpdate

Source: Google is about to remove free access to Gemini Flash and Pro

item.title: AI vendors favor capacity-based pricing models
item.description:
AI vendors favor capacity-based pricing models

A Bain & Company report finds that around 80% of software vendors introducing AI pricing are adopting capacity-based models over pure consumption-based pricing.

🔍 Overview

Capacity-based pricing is emerging as the preferred model for AI software vendors, with approximately four in five opting for fixed commitments rather than charging based on actual usage.

⚙️ Key details

  • Capacity models allow customers to commit to a fixed amount of AI usage for a set period, with no refunds or carry-forward for unused capacity.
  • This approach provides customers with predictable budgets and vendors with stable revenue.
  • The model retains economic advantages of traditional seat-based pricing, as vendors receive revenue from committed entitlements even if unused.
  • Procurement teams and CFOs benefit from defined commitments, avoiding open-ended variable costs.

📊 Pricing trends

  • About 20% of AI-native software companies still rely mainly on per-seat licensing, often supplemented with usage entitlements.
  • Most companies expanding beyond seat-based pricing are adding new pricing meters rather than replacing seats entirely.
  • Among hybrid AI pricing models:
    • Output-based: ~55%
    • Effort-based: ~35%
    • Outcome-based: ~10%

💡 Why it matters

  • Outcome-based pricing, where vendors are paid for business results, remains limited in scope and is most suitable when outcomes are observable, uniquely attributable to AI, and clearly agreed upon.
  • Direct usage pricing continues to have a role, particularly in infrastructure software and products sold to technical buyers.
  • Capacity-based pricing is likely to remain the favored approach for most enterprise applications.

#AIPricing #SaaS #BainReport #CapacityPricing #EnterpriseAI

Source: Capacity pricing gains ground as 80% of AI software vendors choose fixed commitments: Bain
